final.investment_thesis: The three risk seats split 2-1 for 6.03% with no transaction, and weighing them on the merits rather than the vote confirms that split. The aggressive desk's two pillars are real but only one of them is current. Its fundamental pillar is unrebutted: the FQ3 10-Q shows nine-month revenue +16.1%, gross margin 49.1%, EPS +22.4%, operating cash flow of ~$117B already exceeding all of FY2025, a 30% FCF margin and $62.2B of net cash. That evidence rules out zero exposure — liquidating a cash-generative franchise with a rising 200 SMA at 278.86 (about 11.5% below spot) to save round-trip fees would forfeit a high-quality compounder precisely when its own bear case is only ~3.5% away at the 300.00 first target. But the aggressive desk's own technical pillar contradicts its sizing: it concedes the add trigger is a volume-confirmed close above 318.73, that trigger is ~2.5% above spot and unfired, and the tape it cites as '缩量回调是加仓窗口' is described in the same breath as MACD histogram -3.634 on an up day and volume decaying 75.1M -> 68.0M -> 49.4M. Buying the unconfirmed read is paying up for a signal the desk itself defined and the market has not delivered — that is the weakness, not the strength, of the 12% case. The conservative and neutral desks win the sizing argument because they do not require a directional forecast to justify 6%: the position is a bounded, fee-justified stake with a defined stop at 299.5, sized so a move through 300 toward the 278-280 air pocket costs roughly 0.6% of total equity against roughly 1.0% at 10% and 1.2% at 12%. Downside versus cash opportunity cost is genuinely two-sided and I will not pretend otherwise: $93,871 sits in cash earning no interest, so if AAPL reclaims 318.73 and then the 322-324 VWMA/Bollinger confluence and the unfilled 329.59-333.74 gap, a 6% position contributes only about 0.5% of account return per 3.5-4% move in the stock, and that forgone upside is the explicit price of refusing to press. The higher allocation I am rejecting is 12% (~$11,987, ~$5,963 of added exposure): it is only defensible after a close above 318.73 on volume north of ~65M and a hold of 322-324, and buying it now, ahead of the desk's own trigger, is a bet on an unconfirmed tape with a guide-down and component-cost pressure as the fresh 1-4 week negative. The lower allocation I am rejecting is 0-3% (~$0-3,000): it would trim drawdown toward the 300 then 278-280 path but would round-trip roughly $6,024 of stock for fees, extend the very 15% -> 10% -> 6% proportional-trim pattern this decision exists to break, and abandon the position 11.5% above a rising 200 SMA. The 6% is not an unspecified observation position — observation requires no shares. It is a sized, fee-justified stake contributing roughly ±$60 per 1% move in AAPL to total-account return, held through an unresolved technical test on a business whose cash generation is documented rather than hoped for. What would change the call: a daily close above 318.73 on >65M shares followed by a reclaim of the 322-324 confluence justifies scaling toward 8-10% and would move the rating toward Overweight; a close below 300.00 (hard invalidation 299.5) justifies cutting toward 3% and would move it toward Underweight; and the September quarter must be re-read for gross-margin commentary and the unexplained ~$13B intangible build before the total target changes again. Missing from the record and flagged rather than papered over: the size of the guidance cut is unquantified, news coverage is only 20 of 202 records for 7/29-8/3, CEO succession and the OpenAI litigation impact are not quantified, and no consensus or valuation multiple beyond a rough ~34x annualized-EPS back-of-envelope is supplied — so the price target here is technical, not valuation-derived.
